rules: Daily targets are hard minimums and must not be silently reduced for expected-profit optimization.
A scheduled slot that cannot reach verified publication is not discarded; it becomes publication debt.
Publication debt survives date changes and PC power-off periods until buyer/reader-visible publication is verified.
Previous-day debt must be serviced before treating the current day's quota as satisfied.
One run may complete multiple publications when debt exists; five per catch-up cycle is a pacing preference, not a lifetime or daily production cap.
Do not count queue insertion, local publisher success logs, editor/admin URLs, drafts, commits, or unverified pages as completed publications.
Cloud-side planning, build preparation, queue production and repair continue after 01:00 JST even when the Windows PC is expected to be off.
Windows-dependent note/BOOTH publication should be front-loaded before 01:00 JST; 23:10 and 00:10 are catch-up windows when the PC is available.
If the PC is powered off for an entire calendar day, missed quota is retained as debt and caught up automatically at the next PC-available session.
Do not disable BOOTH/note cloud automation because of a recoverable publication or verification delay.
If one candidate remains blocked, defer it and switch to another qualified candidate rather than ending a production run without a verified publication.
